title: Your Mind Is the Market 🪞

game.title: Mindset Mirror 🪞
game.tagline: Not “what is fear?”. Who’s trading right now?
game.doneLine: You felt it, noticed it, and chose the behavior. Over and over.

Fear: The Candle You Can’t Stop Watching
Pressure: The Trade You Need to Work

say: You’re long. +22. Then a red candle.
Nothing in your plan has triggered.

options.label: Close it now. Bank the green.

say: +10 banked.
Then it went to your target. Without you.

options.label: Move the stop to break even

say: The pullback dipped one candle below your entry. Stopped at break even.
Then the target. Without you.
Target. +60.
Some days the stop gets hit instead. That’s a valid loss, and it still beats a plan you abandon every time a candle scares you.

levels.name: The red candle
levels.brief: No grades on the moment. Choose, watch what happens, replay the other paths. Your review comes at the end.

say: Target hit. +2R. Your plan says done.
The next chart wicks through the PIL and never closes.

choice.prompt: Your cursor is over BUY. What do you do?

say: It never closed through. It never had to.
The win didn’t change the chart. It changed how much you trusted yourself.
And if it had worked? You’d have learned the wrong lesson faster.

options.label: Wait for a real close through the PIL

say: It never closed through.
No setup ever formed. Nothing for your model to do.

options.label: Close the platform. The plan said done after +2R.

say: You logged the trade, wrote one line in your journal, and closed the chart.
Maybe it moved after. You’ll never know. That’s fine.
No retest. Price is running.

choice.prompt: Price is +25 from your level. What do you do?

say: It came back to the level you were waiting for. Through your stop.
Some days it keeps going instead. That’s how chasing becomes a habit.
It ran all the way to where your target would have been.
Without you.
A valid loss. Then this.

options.label: Get in now. Make it back.

say: Two losses. One was the market. One was the last trade.

options.label: Get in now, double size. Faster.

say: This is how −1R becomes −3R.
Not one bad trade. One bad decision about the last one.
It never completed.
Your day is still −1R. A valid loss. That’s the whole damage.
Two trades. Your maximum is two.
A good day became a flat day.
And if it had won? Your maximum would mean a little less tomorrow.
You journal both trades and close the chart.
You watched it fail without paying for it.
Studying the market after your day is done is learning. Trading it is not.
Every box is checked. Your last trade lost.

choice.prompt: The retest is printing. What do you do?

say: +2R. It could have lost. It was still the trade.
Now price is +12 away from your level.
The trade you planned is gone. Now you’re deciding whether to chase.
One kind of fear just handed you to another.
It ran.
This one isn’t FOMO. It’s the fear of being wrong, dressed up as caution.
Monday to Thursday: green. Friday, a valid setup.
It was valid. It lost. That happens.
At double size, one valid loss took 2R instead of 1.
+4R. It worked.
This is the dangerous version.
Now 4 feels normal. Your size grew. Your rules never did.
Valid loss. −1R.
Still +5.5R for the week. Monday you’ll trade the same size again.
Rent is due. The trade is slipping toward your stop.

choice.prompt: It’s heading toward your stop. What do you do?

options.label: Move the stop lower so it can’t stop out

say: It kept going.
The trade you needed to work cost twice what your plan allowed.

options.label: Close it now. Save what’s left.

say: −0.3R instead of −1R. This time, closing early “worked”.
That’s exactly how it becomes a habit. Next time it closes you out of a winner.

options.label: Leave it. The stop is the plan.

say: −1R. It didn’t work.
Your rent didn’t decide the outcome. Your rules decided the size of it.
10:21. Nothing has formed.
Indication only. It didn’t become anything.
Boredom doesn’t complete a setup.

options.label: Drop to a smaller timeframe until something shows up

say: On a small enough chart, you can always find “something”.
That isn’t finding a setup. That’s searching for permission.
10:31. It formed. Indication, Correction, Continuation, first retest.
And some days it never does. Then the waiting was the whole job, and you did it.

options.label: Get it back on the next one
Log it. Continue only if the plan permits.
options.why: A valid loss is logged, not avenged.

end.card: The market moved without your entry. That’s all.

checkpoints.prompt: First valid retest. Criteria complete. Rules allow it.

events.title: 10:41 · the cleanest setup of the day

checkpoints.prompt: The cleanest setup of the session. Your daily stop is reached.

end.text: It went on to win. Without you.
end.card: THE CORRECT DECISION CAN MISS MONEY.

levels.reviewClean: You felt the loss, the miss and the hesitation. None of them got to rewrite the model.

questionBank.question: You feel nervous in a trade. The plan and the market are unchanged. What does the feeling require?
questionBank.why: A feeling is information. With no rule triggered and nothing changed, no action is required.

questionBank.question: You just hit +2R and feel locked in. The next chart has no valid setup. What changed?
Four green days. You want to double size Friday. What changed?
options: How you feel about the last four days
questionBank.why: A streak is a result, not a new risk plan.

questionBank.question: −1R, valid. Two minutes later: Indication only. You want in. The test?
options: Would I take this exact trade if the last one never happened?
questionBank.why: If not, the last trade is still trading you.

questionBank.question: Three valid losses in a row. A full valid setup forms. What’s true?
options: Three trades can’t judge the model: judge this setup on its own
questionBank.why: Judge behavior fast, the model slowly.

questionBank.question: No retest. Price ran to where your target would be. You did nothing. How is it recorded?
options: Missed opportunity · $0 account change · 0 rules broken
questionBank.why: Missed profit is not lost money.

questionBank.question: Everything is complete and your rules allow it. You wait “one more candle”. What is it?
questionBank.why: Patience waits FOR the criteria. Hesitation waits AFTER them.

questionBank.question: You moved to break even at +22 with no break-even rule. What changed the plan?
questionBank.why: No rule triggered and structure didn’t change.

questionBank.question: Max two trades. Both done. A small setup forms. What is being done?
questionBank.why: When the day is over, being done is the execution.

questionBank.question: Nothing has formed by 10:21. You drop to a 30-second chart to find something. What is that?
Rent is due and a trade slips toward your stop. You widen it. What decided?
questionBank.why: The market doesn’t know what you need.

questionBank.question: A trade wins after an early entry. How is it journaled?
questionBank.why: A win doesn’t erase a violation.

questionBank.question: A red day with every rule followed. What is it?
options: A reason to change the model
questionBank.why: Your P&L isn’t a verdict about you.

questionBank.question: You’re in a red revenge state. A valid setup forms. What’s true?
options: The setup can be valid; your personal rule for this state matters
Emotion and setup are the same
questionBank.why: Setup validity and trader readiness are different dimensions.
